battle.name: 趙萬海起義
battle.brief: 大業十二年冬，隋廷主力西征高句麗未歸、關中河北大饑，渤海郡樂安縣丞趙萬海糾集縣兵與潰卒據城起事，一度威脅郡治；竇建德遣兵策應，翌年進取樂安，趙萬海部眾自此併入夏軍。卡面羅馬投石機未隨軍而至，但起義方攻城守城所用的拋石車、撞車與強弩，同屬以配重拋射巨石破壞城垣的器械譜系。

kit.name: 投石機
kit.history: 把絞盤的勢能換成一塊石頭。攻城從此有了可以計算的破壞力。

countries: 這場衝突是隋朝末年河北渤海郡一帶的地方起事，發生在隋煬帝大業十二年（616）冬，背景是第三次征高句麗之後的軍隊崩潰與關中山東的饑荒。朝廷一方是隋朝中央與渤海郡的地方官署：行軍尚書、行軍長史以下各府縣分守，郡丞主縣務、郡尉掌兵，郡兵之外另有鄉兵與屯田客，這些武裝是關防的唯一依賴。起事一方以樂安縣丞趙萬海為首，糾集縣兵、逃亡潰卒與無糧可食的鄉民，據樂安城自守，之後與渤海郡另一支起義首領竇建德互相策應；竇建德於大業十三年（617）攻取樂安，趙萬海部眾自此併入竇建德建立的夏政權。北面同時存在劉黑闥等河北起義武裝，以及契丹、靺鞨、高句麗等邊患，隋廷兵力四面分散，無力單獨平定任何一處。關於本役的原始記錄十分零散，現存可考的只有起事人物、可能的接應者與大致的地域，兵員編制多賴《隋書》《北史》與《資治通鑑》相關年代條目互相參證，確切番次與官銜已難盡考。
countriesEn: This conflict was a local rising in the Bohai Commandery area of Hebei in northern China, breaking out in the winter of the twelfth year of the Daye era (616), against a background of the collapse of the Sui field army after the third expedition against Goguryeo and of famine in the passes of Guanzhong and in Shandong. On the court side stood the Sui central government together with the local offices of Bohai Commandery: below the Commissioner of the March and the Chief Administrative Officer of the March, each prefecture and county held its own ground, the Assistant Prefect of the Commandery handled county administration, the Commandery Guard Commander held the troops, and beyond the regular county soldiers there were local militia and garrison settlers — these armed groups were the only defensive resource available. The insurgents were led by Zhao Wanhai, Assistant Prefect of Le'an County, who gathered county soldiers, deserters and hungry villagers and held the city of Le'an; he then coordinated with the other insurgent leader in Bohai Commandery, Dou Jiande, who took Le'an in the thirteenth year of Daye (617), after which Zhao Wanhai's men were folded into the Xia regime Dou had founded. To the north other armed bands such as those of Liu Heita were on the rise at the same time, alongside frontier pressure from Khitan, Mohe and Goguryeo, so Sui forces were stretched in every direction and unable to suppress any one of these risings. The original record of this rising is extremely fragmentary: what survives establishes only the identity of the rebel leader, the likely supporter, and the rough geography, while the details of unit organisation must be reconstructed by cross-reading the relevant annals of the History of Sui, the History of Northern Dynasties and the Comprehensive Mirror; the exact establishment numbers and the precise ranks of those involved can no longer be fully verified.
people: 起事的核心人物是趙萬海。他是隋朝樂安縣丞，屬郡府低階但實際主持一縣軍政的官員，掌縣內兵籍、糧械與城守；正因為職權在手，他才有能力在郡兵空虛、糧道斷絕的時節一呼而集。關於他的出身與早年經歷，現存史料留下的記載極少，只能確定他不是史傳留名的宿將，而是亂世中由郡吏脫身而成的一方首領。與他並肩的是渤海郡的起義首領竇建德：竇建德出身農家，因河北饑荒聚眾自保，先據渤海郡樂壽、照城一帶，自稱夏王，置官屬，與隋廷對抗；趙萬海起事之後，竇建德曾遣兵策應並於翌年進取樂安，兩人由並肩作戰轉為上下相屬。朝廷方面的關鍵人物是隋煬帝楊廣，他在大業十二年仍以江都為行在，先前親統大軍第三次征高句麗，至是年十月病逝江都，帝死而後天下益無統一號令之樞。河北方面尚有劉黑闥等武裝首領乘時並起。隋朝郡將校尉的姓名、趙萬海陣中的指揮分派，以及雙方往來交涉的經過，史料皆未詳載。
peopleEn: The central figure of the rising was Zhao Wanhai. He was Assistant Prefect of Le'an County under the Sui — a junior official of the commandery administration who in practice directed the military affairs of a whole county, holding its muster rolls, its grain and ordnance, and its city defences. Precisely because that authority was in his hands he was able to rally a following in a moment when the commandery troops were absent and the grain road was cut. Very little survives about his origins or early career; what can be established is that he was not a famous general with a biography, but a local official of the commandery who broke away and became a leader of his own in a collapsing age. Standing beside him was Dou Jiande, the insurgent chief of Bohai Commandery: a peasant's son who, in the Hebei famine, gathered a band to feed himself, first establishing himself around Leshou and Zhaocheng in Bohai Commandery, proclaiming himself King of Xia, setting up officials and offices, and making war on the Sui court. After Zhao Wanhai rose, Dou sent troops to support him and in the following year advanced upon Le'an, so that the two men moved from being equals in arms to a superior and subordinate relationship. The decisive figure on the court side was Emperor Yang of Sui, Yang Guang, who still kept Jiangdu as his travelling seat in the twelfth year of Daye and had personally led the third expedition against Goguryeo; he fell ill and died at Jiangdu in the tenth month of that year, and with the emperor gone the empire had no single seat of authority left to give orders. On the Hebei side, armed leaders such as Liu Heita rose at the same time. The names of the Sui commandery commanders, the division of command within Zhao Wanhai's ranks, and the course of any negotiations between the two sides are all absent from the historical record.
kits: 卡面這件羅馬投石機並不屬於616年中原戰場的裝備，它是西元前250年前後羅馬城邦用於圍城的單臂擲石機：以木構機架固定在底座上，一支長臂架在配重之上，發射時靠配重下沉把石彈拋向城牆，專打城頭守軍、塔樓與城門上方，用以在強攻前先削薄防禦。但它所對應的器械譜系在同期中國完全存在。隋代攻城所用的拋石車，漢魏史書稱為「石砲」「霹靂車」，形制與onager同屬以配重換取投射距離的擲石機，架設在牛車或木架之上，發射前以人力與畜力拉緊機括，拋出數十至百餘斤的巨石，專打城頭女牆與敵陣密集之處。中國的拋石車以石為彈，就地取來的山石反覆可射，勝在經得起持久圍城，與羅馬砲的陶製圓彈路子相近。除拋石之外，隋代攻城還有撞車、穴車、雲梯、巢車、飛石、蒙革的破障車，以及火油火箭等一整套器械；守城一方則倚城頭檑木礌石、手投礟石，並以臂弩、床弩與天子弩等強弩封鎖城門與壕溝。兵員裝備以明光鎧、兜鍪、長柄大刀、直刀、馬槊、皮盾為主，騎兵用於切斷糧道與追擊潰散之敵。戰馬、牛車與糧車構成後勤主力，攻城塔車與蒙甲的破障車則隨主力緩行。
kitsEn: The Roman onager shown on the card was not equipment present on a mid-sixteenth-century Chinese battlefield. It is the single-armed stone thrower used by the Roman republic and early empire in siege operations from around 250 BC: a wooden frame fixed to a base, a long arm rested on a counterweight, and on firing the descent of the counterweight that throws the stone at the curtain wall, aimed at the defenders on the parapet, at towers and at the space above the gates, so as to thin the defences before an assault. The lineage of the machine, however, existed in China in the same period in full. The stone-throwing cart used by Sui siege armies, called a stone catapult or a thunder-thrower in Han and Wei histories, belongs to the same family as the onager: a weight-driven stone thrower mounted on a cart or timber frame, wound up by men and draught animals before firing and hurling stones of tens to more than a hundred catties, aimed at the parapet and at massed enemy troops. The Chinese machines used stone as their missile; rock gathered on the spot could be fired again and again, which suited a protracted siege, much as Roman artillery reused its round shot. Beside the stone throwers, the Sui siege train included battering rams, burrowing carts, scaling ladders, tower carts, hand-thrown stones, hide-covered assault vehicles, and fire-arrows tipped with burning oil. The defenders relied on logs and rocks dropped from the parapet, on hand-thrown stones, and on the arm crossbows, bed crossbows and heavy crossbows that sealed the gates and the ditch. On the soldiers' side the main items were bright-armour cuirasses, helmets, long-handled sabres, straight swords, cavalry lances, and leather shields; the cavalry was used to cut supply lines and pursue routed men. Warhorses, ox-carts and grain wagons formed the logistical backbone, while siege towers and armoured assault vehicles advanced slowly with the main body.
tactics: 起事的第一步是抓空檔。大業十二年，隋廷主力陷在遼東，樂安一縣的郡兵多被徵發西去，縣城只剩下老弱與少量縣卒，糧食又因連年歉收與漕運斷絕而告罄，趙萬海據此選擇夜間舉事，以自己掌握的縣兵為骨幹，令潰卒與饑民分持兵器雜械，內應而外合，先取縣城，再據城以自固。守城時他倚城頭高處施檑木礌石，招募鄉勇輪番執飛石向逼近的官軍投擲，強弩封住城門與壕溝，把重點放在遲滯官軍的衝鋒，避免在城門洞開之際被一次突破。官軍若反過來攻城，則拋石車先行，置於城外安全距離，專打城頭守軍與女牆，掩護撞車抵門、穴車掘進、雲梯靠牆；步兵以蒙革的車為掩蔽，分番更替，白日進逼、夜間襲營。竇建德的策應重在輕騎：其部眾不急於攻城，而先斷糧道、迫郡兵分兵，並在官軍疲於應戰時合兵進取。補給線是這支起義軍最脆弱的一環：糧食全賴鄉里就地搜括，遇上饑年只能流動求生；隋軍則倚江都、洛陽輻輳，遠道運糧極難，一旦郡兵被圍而援兵不至，守城一方往往先耗盡。
tacticsEn: The first step of the rising was to seize the moment of vacancy. In the twelfth year of Daye the Sui main army was bogged down in Liaodong, most of the commandery troops of Le'an had been conscripted westward, the county city was left with the old, the weak and a handful of local soldiers, and grain had run out through repeated bad harvests and the severance of the canal transport. Zhao Wanhai accordingly chose to rise at night. Using the county soldiers under his own command as the backbone, he armed deserters and hungry villagers with whatever weapons and tools they had, and struck from within and without at once, taking the county city first and then holding it. In defence he used the height of the rampart to drop logs and rocks, enrolled local braves to take turns hurling stones at the approaching government troops, and sealed the gates and the ditch with crossbows, concentrating on blunting the momentum of assaults rather than risking a single breakthrough while the gate stood open. Had the government forces come to storm the city instead, the stone throwers would have led, sited at a safe distance outside the walls and aimed at the parapet and its defenders, covering the rams driven against the gate, the burrowing carts sent in under the wall and the scaling ladders brought up. Infantry would advance behind hide-covered carts, reliefs taking turns, pushing forward by day and raiding the camp by night. Dou Jiande's support lay in his light cavalry: rather than hurrying to storm the walls, his men cut the grain road, forced the commandery troops to divide, and closed in only when the government troops were exhausted by constant answering of alarms. Supply was the weakest link in the insurgent force: food came entirely from foraging the countryside, and in a lean year the band had to keep moving to survive. Sui troops, by contrast, drew on Jiangdu and Luoyang, and long-distance grain supply was extremely difficult; once a commandery garrison was surrounded with no relieving force coming, the defenders of the city were usually the first to be exhausted.
data: 關於數字，可靠的只有幾組。隋朝鼎盛時的戶口，據《隋書·地理志》計，全州郡合計戶八百九十餘萬，丁四百六十餘萬；歷經三次征高句麗與關內大旱，到大業末年只剩一半上下。人口銳減的背景是饑荒：《資治通鑑》記大業末年江淮之間米價飛騰、饑民採橡實與樹皮，甚至出現人相食的慘狀，河北山東受害尤重。軍事的時間點也清楚：第三次征高句麗自大業十年末打到十二年，隋軍主力回師途中局勢已崩；大業十二年（616）十月，隋煬帝楊廣在江都病死；十三年（617）竇建德在渤海郡建國稱夏王；同年樂安落入夏軍；武德三年（621）五月，虎牢關一役李世民以精騎數千擊破竇建德前鋒，記斬首三千餘級，隨後夜襲牛口渚，竇建德被俘，軍中降者數萬，河北遂定。趙萬海本人所能掌握的兵員則沒有可靠數字：樂安為一縣之地，可供驅使的縣兵與潰卒當在數千上下，起義能夠打成，靠的是郡兵空虛而非兵力優勢，這一點從戰果與持續時間便可看出。
dataEn: As to figures, only a few groups are reliable. At the height of Sui the household registers recorded in the Geography Treatise of the History of Sui give, for all the provinces and commanderies combined, a little over 8.9 million households and some 4.6 million able-bodied men; after three campaigns against Goguryeo and the great drought in the passes, by the end of the Daye era barely half of that remained. The background to the population collapse was famine: the Comprehensive Mirror records that in the last years of Daye the price of rice in the Jianghuai region rocketed, the hungry ate acorns and bark, and there were cases of people eating one another; Hebei and Shandong suffered worst. The chronology of the military events is also clear. The third expedition against Goguryeo ran from the end of the tenth year of Daye into the twelfth, and the situation had already collapsed before the main Sui force began its return; in the tenth month of the twelfth year (616) Emperor Yang of Sui fell ill and died at Jiangdu; in the thirteenth year (617) Dou Jiande founded his state in Bohai Commandery and proclaimed himself King of Xia; in that same year Le'an fell to the Xia forces; in the fifth month of the third year of Wude (621), at the Battle of Hulao, Li Shimin broke Dou Jiande's vanguard with several thousand picked cavalry, the record giving more than three thousand heads taken, and then struck at Niukou at night, capturing Dou Jiande, with tens of thousands surrendering, and Hebei was settled. There is, however, no dependable figure for the troops Zhao Wanhai himself could command: Le'an was a single county, so the county soldiers and deserters he could muster must have numbered a few thousand at most, and the rising succeeded because the commandery troops were absent, not because of any numerical superiority — a point visible from the results achieved and from how long the resistance lasted.
cause: 起事的第一層原因是國家已經轉不動了。大業年間，隋煬帝三次征高句麗，役夫與戰兵被一役接一役地從遼東抽走，河北與山東的丁壯大量外流，農事失耕；其後江淮大旱、運河漕運又被戰事與徵集切斷，糧價一漲再漲，郡縣倉庫空了，饑民成群結隊離鄉。這使得任何一個有兵權的郡吏都有可乘之機。第二層原因是中央權威在地理上離地方太遠：煬帝的行在在涿郡、江都之間巡行，帶走精銳宿衛，留守各郡的多是老弱，郡丞一級的官員實際上獨負一方軍政。第三層原因是軍隊已經解體。逃兵、降卒與被解散的役夫散在鄉里，手中仍有器械與技藝，只要有人出面號召，一夜之間便可成軍。趙萬海既握樂安縣兵籍，又熟悉城守與糧械，在這樣的時局下舉事，並非出於深謀遠慮的籌劃，更像是亂世之中一個地方官員被迫做的抉擇：與其坐看城破人散，不如先取一縣自立。他舉兵之後並非孤軍，竇建德在渤海郡的壯大，使河北的零星起事得以互相接應，這才是這場起義能延續到617年的關鍵。至於趙萬海起義是否另有更深的原因，例如與隋廷內部的傾軋或地方派系有關，現存史料沒有留下線索。
causeEn: The first layer of cause is that the state had stopped working. Through the years of the Daye era Emperor Yang of Sui campaigned against Goguryeo three times, and labour and soldiers were drawn off to Liaodong campaign after campaign; the able-bodied men of Hebei and Shandong left in great numbers and the fields went untilled. Then a great drought struck the Jianghuai, the canal transport was cut by the wars and by fresh levies, the price of grain rose again and again, the granaries of the commanderies and counties stood empty, and the hungry left their homes in bands. Any local official who still held troops could exploit that. The second layer is that central authority stood geographically too far from the localities: the emperor's travelling seat moved between Zhuojun and Jiangdu, taking the elite guards with it, while the commanderies were left with the old and the weak, so an official of the rank of Assistant Prefect in practice bore the whole military burden of his district alone. The third layer is that the army had come apart. Deserters, surrendered men and discharged conscript labourers were scattered across the countryside, still holding their weapons and their training; once someone called them together, an armed force could exist overnight. Zhao Wanhai held the muster rolls of Le'an and knew the city defences and the stores; raising troops in such circumstances was less a deep and far-seeing plan than the choice forced on a local official in a collapsing age: rather than sit and watch the city fall and the people scatter, take one county and stand. He was not alone once he rose. The growth of Dou Jiande in Bohai Commandery allowed the scattered risings in Hebei to support one another, and that is the key to why this rising could still be fighting in 617. Whether Zhao Wanhai's revolt had any deeper cause — friction inside the Sui court, or a local faction — left no trace in the surviving sources.
impact: 對河北而言，這場起義是一次地方秩序崩解的實測：當郡兵主力被抽往遼東，郡守、郡丞這些文官實際上就是當地唯一能組織武裝的人。趙萬海事後被竇建德收編，等於示範了一條路徑——不必等外部大軍到來，地方武裝自己就能攻城略地、自己就能立政權。竇建德自此聲勢更盛，兩年之間盡取河北諸州郡，與唐軍在河北形成拉鋸；同時隋廷的中央權威在616年十月隋煬帝病逝江都之後急劇崩解，關中另立新君、江都另立新帝，617年竇建德稱夏、618年宇文化及弒逆，隋室在趙萬海舉兵之後三年之內名存實亡。就更長的視角看，河北鄉兵與郡兵在隋末普遍被各類武裝吸收，唐朝平定河北後收其精銳充入禁軍與邊軍，使這批原屬地方州郡的武力改隸中央，成為唐初軍制的底子之一。在器械史上，拋石車這類以配重換取射程的重型攻城器械，在隋末群雄爭奪城邑時已被普遍配備，攻城從此更多倚重器械破壞而非單純蟻附，羅馬onager所代表的擲石機譜系，在中國這一時期正是以「砲」與「車」的名義延續下來。
impactEn: For Hebei, this rising was a practical demonstration that the local order had come apart: once the main body of the commandery troops had been pulled off to Liaodong, the prefect and the assistant prefect — men of the civil service — were in fact the only people in the district able to organise armed force. Zhao Wanhai's later absorption by Dou Jiande demonstrated a path: without waiting for a great army from outside, a local armed force could take cities and provinces and could found a government of its own. Dou Jiande grew stronger in consequence, taking the commanderies of Hebei within two years and holding a seesaw war with Tang there. At the same time, the central authority of the Sui court collapsed rapidly after the death of Emperor Yang at Jiangdu in the tenth month of 616, with a new emperor enthroned in Guanzhong and another at Jiangdu; Dou proclaimed Xia in 617 and Yuwen Huaji committed the coup in 618, so that within three years of Zhao Wanhai's raising of troops the Sui house was a name and nothing more. From a longer perspective, the village militia and commandery soldiers of Hebei were absorbed in large numbers by every kind of armed band in the late Sui; after Tang had pacified Hebei it took the picked men of these forces into the imperial guard and the frontier armies, so that military strength formerly belonging to the local commanderies passed under central control and became one of the foundations of early Tang military organisation. In the history of siegecraft, heavy machines like the stone thrower, which bought range through counterweight, were in general issue among the contending warlords of the late Sui as they fought for walled cities, and assaults came to rely more on the destruction wrought by machines than on men simply scaling the walls; the lineage of the stone thrower that the Roman onager represents continued in China at this time precisely under the names of the catapult and the siege cart.
result: 就本役的過程而言，結果是起事成功、然後被併吞。趙萬海在大業十二年冬夜取樂安縣城，憑城固守，隋廷派來的郡兵一時不能克；竇建德見其能久持，乃遣兵策應並於大業十三年進取樂安，趙萬海選擇歸附，縣兵與器械一併納入夏軍，他本人則在夏的官署中獲得職位，身份由一縣之長變為一方將佐。真正的終結在虎牢關：武德三年（621）五月，李世民率精騎在成皋以西擊破竇建德前鋒，夜襲牛口渚，竇建德被俘，隨軍諸將一併淪陷，趙萬海所部亦在此役中潰散，河北於數月之內盡歸唐軍。竇建德被押送京師之後，隋末最大的割據勢力之一從此消失，唐朝得以在關東建立直接統治，樂安一帶的郡縣建制重新編入州府體系。關於趙萬海的下場，史料記載殘缺：可以確定的是他隨竇建德的覆亡而失去全部根基，此後是被誅、被貶抑還是不知所終，各書均無可據之文，本篇只能止於此，不再推衍。
resultEn: As to the course of the rising, the result was that it succeeded and was then swallowed up. Zhao Wanhai took the county city of Le'an on a night in the winter of the twelfth year of Daye and held it behind its walls; the commandery troops sent by the court could not take it for a time. Dou Jiande, seeing that the place could be held, sent troops to support him and in the thirteenth year of Daye advanced upon Le'an; Zhao Wanhai chose to submit, his county soldiers and their ordnance being taken over into the Xia army, while he himself received an office in Xia's bureaucracy, changing from the head of a single county into an officer of a state. The real ending came at Hulao: in the fifth month of the third year of Wude (621) Li Shimin broke Dou Jiande's vanguard with picked cavalry west of Chenggao, struck Niukou by night and captured Dou Jiande; the commanders who went with him were taken along with him, and the troops of Zhao Wanhai broke up in the same battle, so that within a few months all of Hebei fell to the Tang army. Once Dou Jiande had been escorted to the capital, one of the largest separatist powers of the late Sui disappeared for good, and the Tang could set up direct government east of the passes, with the commanderies and counties of the Le'an area folded once more into the regular prefectural system. As for Zhao Wanhai's own fate, the record is fragmentary: what can be established is that he lost every footing with the fall of Dou Jiande, and whether he was executed, banished or simply disappeared from the pages is not supported by any text; this account stops there and draws no further inference.
